monument_name: Khām stone memorial pillars (ca. 13th to 16th century)
description_en: The Khām stone memorial pillars, which date from 13th to 16th century, are located on a mountain ridge above the village of Khām, which can be reached from Lekhpur (see Lekhpur Lāmā Banthān,JUM0540). The name 'Khām' is derived from the termkhambā, which means "pillar". The carvings on the pillars have eroded. Pillar 002, is located 700 meters to the south of Pillar 001. Its decoration features astūpa, surmounted by a rosetta. Locals refer to Pillar 002 as Okharpate Khambā. According to legend, if people from Okharpate (a village on a hill across the Sinja valley, north-west of Khām) saw this pillar, they would die.From the 13th to the 17th centuries, stone memorial pillars were erected throughout the Karnali Basin. They are erected to honour war heroes (Andolfatto 2019). In Khām, there are no inscriptions on any of the pillars. Their typology suggests that they were erected between the 13th and the 16th century.
monument_assessment: Slightly damaged (minor damages such as minor cracks, plants, missing stones in plinths), Surface damages
references: REFERENCES Andolfatto, David C. 2019. Le Pays aux Cent-Vingt-Cinq-Mille Montagnes. Etude Archéologique du Bassin de la Karnali (Népal) entre le XIIe et le XVIe siècle . Paris: Sorbonne Université.
